instrument: Minn. Stat. § 462.355, subd. 4(d), as applied in the Inver Grove Heights interim ordinance
summary: An interim ordinance (moratorium) alone may not halt, delay or impede a subdivision with preliminary approval, nor unilaterally extend the § 15.99 review timelines for an application filed before the ordinance takes effect. Minnesota interim ordinances may run up to 12 months and cannot be used solely to delay or prevent a single project.

source.citation: City of Inver Grove Heights, June 22/26, 2026 council packet, Item 7.D (interim ordinance text; litigation counsel memo; developer counsel letter)

confidence_note: Read in the ordinance text that restates the statute; the statute itself not read.
text: nor may it unilaterally extend the timelines set forth in Minnesota Statutes, Section 15.99 with respect to any application filed prior to the effective date of the Ordinance
